newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rights group urges speedy Hong Kong elections.
newsitem.headline: Rights group urges speedy Hong Kong elections.

text.p: Human rights in Hong Kong may be in "jeopardy" if China-backed new rulers delay calling elections, an international human rights group said on Friday.
Washington-based Human Rights Watch/Asia urged Hong Kong's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, to defer any new legislation that might affect civil liberties until after fresh polls.
China will replace Hong Kong's partially-elected legislative council with a hand-picked provisional assembly when it takes back the British colony on July 1.
Hong Kong's future government has pledged to hold elections within a year, under rules still to be agreed.

"The decision to dissolve the Legislative Council means that as of July 1, the people of Hong Kong are effectively deprived of their right to participate in government through freely chosen representatives," said Sidney Jones, executive director of Human Rights Watch/Asia.

"The longer the wait until new elections, the more serious the problem becomes, especially since the appointed legislators have already approved amendments that will curtail basic freedoms. If they continue to do so, human rights may be in real jeopardy," Jones said in a statement.

The Beijing-appointed Provisional Legislative Council has already vowed to strike down some laws on civil liberties, arguing that they contravene the Basic Law, Hong Kong's post-handover mini-constitution.
